ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. derivation: Three limits compose, restated without the v1 errors. (1) Replay limit, corrected: H5 (deterministic replay) plus H8 (third-party recompute) require the committed output to be a function of frozen inputs alone; an execution whose result depends on physical interleaving is unreplayable. The boundary is DETERMINISM OF OUTCOME, which is achievable two ways: (i) commuting-effect antichains with a deterministic merge order (Church-Rosser confluence), and (ii) deterministic conflict-ordered execution — pre-committing a serialization order and executing non-commuting stages concurrently under mechanisms that guarantee the outcome equals that order's serial result. Route (ii) demonstrably admits MORE concurrency than the commutativity bound while remaining a pure function of frozen inputs, so the v1 claim 'no feasible system can admit more concurrency than the commuting fraction' is retracted; the ceiling is the deterministic-outcome frontier. (2) Scheduling limit: the work-span law T_p >= max(T_1/p, T_inf) is information-flow arithmetic on the DAG; under H6 speculative state may never become visible in the trusted store, so speculation can discard work but not beat the span bound. (3) Arbitration limit, with the FLP misuse struck: FLP bounds deterministic consensus in the fully asynchronous faulty model only; it caps neither a single-authority model (where no consensus is needed) nor partially-synchronous BFT total ordering (feasible and in production). The arbitration ceiling is a deterministic decidable admission predicate evaluated at the single logical serialization point; on a single-authority operating model, kernel-DAC enforcement below the code is the strongest available seat; on a multi-authority model, a machine-checked nonforking replicated total order is strictly stronger in operator-independence at declared consensus-resource cost. H3 forces failure semantics: a failed stage cannot be marked executed; the only fail-closed option is atomic tier abort with exact pre-tier state (ties to AX-11).

ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. The maximum feasible institutional decision authority under H1-H8 is: every trusted state transition is admitted by one total, pure, decidable kernel predicate K(state, transition, certificate) evaluated at the single logical serialization point, where acceptance yields a certificate-carrying, sequence-monotonic transition and EVERY other outcome — including an error inside the gate's own predicates — is a recorded, signed refusal with zero state change (fail-closed totality); authorization validity is offline-decidable by any third party recomputing the capability/delegation chain from a committed genesis trust anchor, which no system can eliminate (signatures transfer trust, they cannot create it); machine authority extends exactly to authorization and process compliance, never to the substantive rightness of the institutional decision itself, which remains with the accountable human creator; and [RESOURCE_BOUNDED equivocation clause] absent an external witness quorum — a deployment resource operationally available today, not an unreachable one — equivocation resistance is capped at fork consistency: a lying single writer can maintain divergent views, but any two views that ever meet yield producer-attributable cryptographic evidence (two signed checkpoints for the same sequence); enrolling a cosigning witness quorum lifts the cap to split-view resistance.
derivation: (1) Verification theory: an offline verifier (H8) checks only decidable predicates over committed bytes; accountable authority is maximized exactly when admission IS a decidable proof-checking problem — any authority not reified as a checkable certificate is unverifiable assertion, rated zero by H8. (2) Trust-anchor necessity: every signature chain terminates in a key whose bindingness is an axiom; a verifier with no prior trusted bit authenticates nothing; the ceiling is a minimal, committed, explicit genesis anchor, not its elimination. (3) Fail-closed totality (H2+H3): an erring gate predicate has produced UNKNOWN, which never upgrades to pass; the ceiling gate maps every non-proof path to a refusal that is itself a derivation (which conjunct, over which committed facts), durably recorded; 'never wrongly refuse' would require deciding properties of arbitrary future predicates (Rice), so refusal stays cheap, recorded, and creator-overridable only via an explicit reason-carrying logged override. (4) Equivocation bound (SUNDR), relabeled: with a single writer and no independent witnesses, fork consistency is the provable maximum; full split-view resistance requires an external cosigning quorum. That quorum is a DEPLOYMENT RESOURCE — witness networks with shared vetted configurations operate across ecosystems today, so the v1 phrase 'not within unilateral reach today' is retracted; by the corpus's own labeling standard (a resource that would strictly lift the cap, excluded only by declared scope) this clause is RESOURCE_BOUNDED. Auditability terminates at the commitment boundary: nothing outside the committed closure (e.g., what the publisher's server really served at capture time) is auditable in principle — the strongest attainable is a signed/witnessed/channel-attested capture receipt committing the bytes at ingestion. COST clause (RESOURCE_BOUNDED): linear-cost recomputation is the operative verification cost only for a declared toolchain lacking an arithmetization of its pipeline; a transparent proof toolchain strictly lowers verifier cost with no assurance loss.
derivation: Verification theory admits exactly two zero-trust offline verification modes: recompute-and-compare, and proof-checking. The v1 dismissal of mode (b) is corrected on two counts: (1) it rested on a false cryptographic premise — transparent (STARK-class) proof systems have NO trusted setup; their assumptions are collision-resistant hashing, the same family the ceilings already accept for SHA-256 commitments — so mode (b) adds no new trust CATEGORY, only a proof-system soundness reduction within the same family; (2) 'arithmetizing the pipeline is infeasible' is a toolchain/cost fact, which may not appear inside an ABSOLUTE label — it is carved into the RESOURCE_BOUNDED cost clause. H8's semantic content is zero producer trust; both modes satisfy it and are equally maximal in assurance, so 'recompute-and-compare is the ceiling' is restated as 'derivability-from-committed-bytes under stated assumptions is the ceiling, attained by either mode'. The boundary claim is information-theoretic and stands: two histories producing identical committed byte-closures are indistinguishable to any auditor; past states of external sources are not replayable, hence capture receipts (signed, witnessed, or channel-attested per AX-04) are the maximum for origin bytes. Completeness of the closure is capped by what was committed — an audit is exactly as strong as the closure is total.

ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. On the declared operating model (single node, POSIX filesystem, commodity SSD with honored write barriers), the maximum achievable is: (a) DURABILITY — a state transition is durable exactly when its data, metadata, and directory entry have reached stable media behind an explicit write barrier (fsync of file AND containing directory); acknowledged-but-unsynced data is unrecoverable in principle; single-device durability is bounded by media survival — nothing short of replication (outside the declared model, a resource not an impossibility) exceeds it. (b) CRASH CONSISTENCY — atomicity of accountable transitions: after a crash at ANY point, recovery yields a state equal to applying some prefix of the committed transition sequence, with every barrier-acknowledged transition included and no torn/partial artifact ever observable (H6 as a maximum). (c) BOUNDED RECOVERY — recovery work is Theta(uncommitted tail since last checkpoint), capped by checkpointing; no scheme recovers in less than the time to read what recovery must read. (d) FAIL-CLOSED READ-BACK — a transition counts committed only after recompute-and-compare of the persisted bytes (H3/H8).
derivation: Storage physics: volatile memory does not survive power loss, so durability of information not yet behind a stable-media barrier is impossible — the fsync wait is the definition of the durable point on the declared platform. Atomicity: the storage stack provides only small atomic primitives; any larger unit is constructed by a commit protocol requiring at least one ordering barrier between data and commit record; the minimal shape 'intent, data barrier, atomic switch, directory barrier' is what every known correct protocol reduces to (the reduction claim is discharged as the AX-11 obligation, shared). Prefix semantics is the consistency ceiling: a crash lands between any two barriers, so the strongest single-node invariant is 'some committed prefix, monotone, nothing torn'; promising more violates physics, promising less violates H3/H6. Recovery lower bound is counting: recovery must read the journal tail it replays.

ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Under the declared operating model (single node, fair scheduler, eventually-available storage, finite committed inputs, external calls that may fail forever), the maximum achievable liveness is CONDITIONAL BOUNDED TERMINATION: every admitted task reaches, within an explicit per-task budget B(task), exactly one of three terminal states — SUCCESS with certificate, typed FAIL, or typed UNKNOWN/REFUSED — with no livelock, no unbounded retry, and no silent hang; retries are idempotent so a re-attempt after partial failure has exactly-once observable effect on committed state; after a crash, work resumes from the last checkpoint with bounded re-execution. Unconditional liveness is UNACHIEVABLE by any system honoring H3 — blocking on persistent environment misbehavior is forced, and the ceiling converts every such block into a typed, bounded-time refusal rather than a hang.
derivation: (1) Fail-closed vs progress trade-off: H3 requires blocking on error/violation/unknown; an adversarial environment can stall any H3-compliant system indefinitely, so progress is only ever conditional on declared environment assumptions; the maximum is making the condition explicit and the failure mode a bounded-time typed refusal (H2). Safety-preserving systems buy liveness only from environment assumptions. (2) Exactly-once effects: at-least-once retry plus at-most-once effect requires idempotence/deduplication state — exactly-once delivery without a dedup record is classically impossible — so idempotency-keyed retries against a durable journal are the ceiling mechanism. (3) Termination cannot be inferred (halting), so the maximum feasible guarantee is termination BY CONSTRUCTION — every trusted loop carries a well-founded variant, making non-termination structurally impossible rather than tested-for. Bounded recovery follows from AX-15's checkpoint bound.

(4) No silent degradation: markExecuted is only reachable from a stage-success derivation — the failed-marked-executed defect class is unrepresentable.

attainment_witness_appendix.candidate_mechanism: B0 witness seats: autonomy.lisp bounded consecutive errors + agenda checkpointing; run-proofs.sh deterministic fail-closed exits; typed abort conditions (frbr-conditions.lisp); circuit-breaker.lisp bounded external retry. Steps: (1) every executor stage gets a declared step/retry budget and a variant function — agenda strictly shrinks or budget strictly decrements; (2) idempotency keys = SHA-256(stage-id, committed-input hashes) recorded in the durable journal before effects, checked on re-entry; (3) budget exhaustion raises a typed condition propagating to REFUSED (never marked-executed); (4) circuit-breaker timeouts driven by the logical clock seat so liveness decisions replay under H5.
attainment_witness_appendix.b0_gap_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: executor retry is not idempotency-checked (double-apply possible); parallel-executor.lisp marks failed stages executed — liveness bought by silently discarding failures, fail-open, the opposite of typed refusal; circuit-breaker uses :system wall-clock (not replayable); no global termination variant — boundedness is per-mission convention; omega use-default restarts convert failures into synthesized content.
